title: Foreign Data Wrappers (postgres_fdw)
description: Query remote PostgreSQL databases, MySQL, or files as if they were local tables using SQL/MED standard FDWs.

data.text: **Foreign Data Wrappers (FDW)** implement the ANSI SQL/MED (Management of External Data) standard. With `postgres_fdw`, you can query and join tables residing on remote database servers as if they were local tables in your database.

data.title: Federated Query Across Two PostgreSQL Clusters
data.content: Setting up server connection and importing foreign schema.

data.text: postgres_fdw works best when filters and joins are pushed to the remote server so less data crosses the network. `EXPLAIN VERBOSE` shows whether a predicate was pushed down as a remote SQL clause or applied locally after fetching rows. Joining two foreign tables on the same remote server can also be pushed down as a remote join.

data.title: Check what is pushed to the remote
data.content: The remote SQL shown in the plan is the actual query sent to the other server. If the `WHERE` appears there, the filter was pushed down.
data.code:
EXPLAIN (VERBOSE, COSTS false)
SELECT o.id, o.amount
FROM remote_orders AS o
WHERE o.customer_id = 42
  AND o.ordered_at >= DATE '2024-01-01';

-- Foreign Scan on remote_orders
--   Remote SQL: SELECT id, amount, ordered_at, customer_id
--               FROM public.orders
--               WHERE ((customer_id = 42) AND (ordered_at >= '2024-01-01'))

data.title: The planner assumes the network is local
data.text: The local planner estimates the cost of a foreign scan using `fdw_startup_cost` and `fdw_tuple_cost`, which default to values that assume a fast network. On a high-latency link this makes foreign tables look cheaper than they are, so the planner may choose plans that pull far too many rows across the wire. Raise those two costs to match your real network, and keep heavy aggregations on the remote side.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: `postgres_fdw` enables federated SQL queries across distributed databases.
PostgreSQL pushes down `WHERE` filters and sorting to the remote server to minimize network transfer.
Ideal for microservice data consolidation and cross-database reporting.
